items.news_title: India’s Sarvam launches Indus AI chat app as competition heats up
items.news_summary: Indian startup Sarvam launches Indus AI chat app to compete with global players like ChatGPT. The app offers local language support but faces initial capacity limitations.

comic.panel_description: Split panel scene. Left side shows THE TECHIE excitedly showing a phone with 'INDUS AI' on screen to THE COMMON MAN. Right side shows them both waiting, with multiple loading/buffering symbols over their heads and cobwebs forming between them. A sign reads 'Limited Compute Capacity'.
comic.caption: 'Unlimited potential, limited capacity' - The Indian AI Paradox
comic.image_prompt: RK Laxman style black ink line drawing showing two-panel composition. Left panel: enthusiastic young techie in casual shirt showing smartphone to bewildered common man in dhoti-kurta. Right panel: same characters covered in cobwebs and loading symbols, simple desk setting, minimal background details, pure line art treatment, emphasis on facial expressions, clean black strokes on white paper.
comic.negative_prompt: Avoid color, shading, gradients, specific brand logos, real people, corporate symbols, complex backgrounds, photorealism, grayscale, technological details
comic.layout_notes: Two equal horizontal panels, caption centered below, speech bubbles minimal and clear, emphasis on contrast between enthusiasm and waiting

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon satirizes the gap between India's ambitious AI aspirations and current infrastructure limitations. It plays on the irony of launching a competitor to global AI giants while facing basic capacity constraints. The transformation from excitement to endless waiting highlights the practical challenges of scaling technology in emerging markets.

safety_checks.notes: Generic representation of technology adoption challenges, avoids specific criticism of any company or individual

items.news_title: Faculty member assaulted by student during exam at homoeopathic medical college in Kalaburagi
items.news_source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu
items.news_summary: Student caught using phone during exam at homeopathy college assaults professor. College administration refers matter to disciplinary committee.

comic.panel_description: Split panel: Left side shows THE TECHIE frantically typing on phone while seated at exam desk. Right side shows THE BUREAUCRAT (as college administrator) addressing THE COMMON MAN (as concerned parent), with a sign reading 'Homeopathy College' in background. THE BUREAUCRAT holds a file labeled 'Discipline' that's comically tiny, referencing homeopathic dilution.
comic.caption: Don't worry, we'll dilute the punishment to make it more effective
comic.image_prompt: RK Laxman style split-panel editorial cartoon, pure black ink on white. Left panel: young TECHIE character at exam desk with phone. Right panel: BUREAUCRAT character showing tiny file to worried COMMON MAN character. Simple institutional backdrop with 'Homeopathy College' text. Clean line work, no shading, consistent stroke weight throughout.
comic.negative_prompt: No color, no shading, no real people, no actual violence, no medical instruments, no detailed medical references, no gradients, no photographs, no realistic renderings
comic.layout_notes: Caption centered below split panel. Left panel smaller than right panel (2:3 ratio). Clear division line between panels. Text minimal and clearly legible.

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon satirizes the irony of a violent incident at a homeopathy college by playing on the principle of homeopathic dilution where substances become 'stronger' when more diluted. By showing the bureaucrat's comically small disciplinary file, it mocks the institutional response while making a clever connection to homeopathic principles. The split panel contrasts the serious nature of the offense with the seemingly minimal response.

safety_checks.notes: Avoids direct depiction of violence. Uses institutional satire rather than personal mockery. Medical reference is general rather than specific.

items.news_title: RaGa attacks PM Modi over Trump tariff verdict
items.news_summary: After US Supreme Court rules against Trump's tariffs, Indian opposition criticizes PM Modi for rushing into US trade deal that may now be disadvantageous.

comic.panel_description: Split panel showing THE BUREAUCRAT and THE POLITICIAN playing a game of chess. The Bureaucrat smugly moves a piece labeled 'Trade Deal' while the Common Man watches from behind, scratching his head as his pockets are visibly empty. On the chess board, all the white pieces are marked '0%' while black pieces show '10%'.
comic.caption: Checkmate yourself before you negotiate yourself
comic.image_prompt: RK Laxman style single panel with clean black ink lines showing chess game between bureaucrat and politician, Common Man as spectator, chess pieces with percentage markings, stark white background, strong definitive strokes, cross-hatching for depth, no gray tones
comic.negative_prompt: No specific politicians, no Trump, no Modi, no color, no shading, no photos, no realistic portraits, no gradient effects, no watercolor feel, no painterly style
comic.layout_notes: Caption centered below panel, chess board should be prominent in center, Common Man positioned at right corner as observer

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon uses chess as a metaphor for international trade negotiations, suggesting India may have made premature moves without considering long-term consequences. The bureaucrat's smug expression while making a potentially disadvantageous move reflects the criticism of rushing into trade deals. The Common Man's empty pockets symbolize the possible economic impact on ordinary citizens.

safety_checks.notes: Avoids direct criticism of specific leaders, focuses on policy decisions

items.news_title: Ranaweera's four-for leads Sri Lanka to tense win over West Indies
items.news_summary: Sri Lankan women's cricket team wins close match against West Indies, with spinner Ranaweera taking 4 wickets to defend modest total of 240 runs.

comic.panel_description: THE COMMON MAN stands at a cricket ground boundary rope, holding a magnifying glass to his eye while squinting at a tiny cricket ball in the distance. Behind him, THE BUREAUCRAT sits in a folding chair with a scorecard, smugly showing '240' while holding up 10 fingers to indicate the narrow margin of victory.
comic.caption: Sometimes the smallest margins make the biggest difference
comic.image_prompt: Black ink line art showing two figures at cricket ground - THE COMMON MAN in dhoti-kurta with magnifying glass examining distant cricket ball, THE BUREAUCRAT seated smugly with scorecard. Simple clean lines, minimal background showing boundary rope and grass, RK Laxman style hatching for depth.
comic.negative_prompt: No real cricketers, team logos, cricket uniforms with branding, stadium advertisements, color, shading, photos, realistic faces, exact player likenesses
comic.layout_notes: Caption centered below panel, scorecard numbers clearly visible, magnifying glass detail important for visual gag

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon plays on the nail-biting finish where Sri Lanka won by just 10 runs. Using THE COMMON MAN's bewildered examination of the tiny margin through a magnifying glass juxtaposed with THE BUREAUCRAT's smug satisfaction creates humor around how such small differences can determine major victories in cricket. The visual metaphor of the magnifying glass emphasizes the closeness of the match.

safety_checks.notes: Generic cricket scene, no specific players depicted, focuses on match result not individuals
